facts.statement: Plicatodus is a prehistoric cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Xenacanthidae.
facts.quote: Plicatodus is a prehistoric cartilaginous fish in the family Xenacanthidae

facts.statement: The genus Plicatodus was described by Oliver Hampe in 1995.
facts.quote: It was described by Oliver Hampe in 1995

facts.statement: Plicatodus lived in Europe during the late Carboniferous and Early Permian periods.
facts.quote: that lived in Europe during the late Carboniferous and Early Permian Periods

facts.statement: The type locality for the genus Plicatodus is the Saar-Nahe basin.
facts.quote: The type locality for this genus is the Saar-Nahe basin

facts.statement: Fossils of Plicatodus usually consist of scattered teeth, though one partial skeleton preserves the head, dorsal spine, and pectoral girdle.
facts.quote: Plicatodus fossils generally only consist of scattered, isolated teeth, with one exception: a partial skeleton that includes the head, dorsal spine, and pectoral girdle

facts.statement: The type species P. jordani was described from Permian-aged material found in the upper Odernheim Formation of the Saar–Nahe Basin.
facts.quote: P. jordani was described in 1995 from Permian-aged material (the Asselian part of the Cisuralian to be specific) found in the upper Odernheim Formation of the Saar–Nahe Basin

facts.statement: The Odernheim Formation contains molasse deposits ranging from the late Carboniferous to the early Permian periods.
facts.quote: a molasse of freshwater and shallow marine deposits from late Carboniferous to the early Permian Periods

facts.statement: The species P. plicatus was originally described by Karl von Fritsch in 1879 as a member of the genus Orthacanthus.
facts.quote: P. plicatus was originally described as a member of the genus Orthacanthus by Karl von Fritsch in 1879

facts.statement: P. plicatus fossils come from the Kasimovian-aged Slany Formation in the Rakovnik Basin of Bohemia.
facts.quote: It came from the Kasimovian (Carboniferous) aged Slany Formation in the Rakovnik Basin of Bohemia

facts.statement: It is debated whether P. sp. found in Lower Austria represents a third undescribed species or belongs to P. jordani or P. plicatus.
facts.quote: While it may represent an undescribed third species, it may just as well come from P. jordani or P. plicatus
